newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ghana Gold sees potential for large mine.
newsitem.headline: Ghana Gold sees potential for large mine.

text.p: Explorer Ghana Gold Mines Ltd said on Tuesday recent drilling results from the Santreso gold anomaly in the Ashanti region of south-central Ghana indicated the potential for a large scale, low cost mining operation.
"The extent of the strike length of 90 ppb (parts per billion) of soil geochemical anomaly is now at 13.2 kilometres," Ghana Gold Mines managing director William Howe said.
"Now that we can report encouraging results from our exploration, it confirms the potential for large scale, low cost operations," Howe said in a statement.
He said the anomaly remained open to the northeast with mineralisation confirmed at Nyabo and Nyabo East, located along the same trend four km north east of the Konongo town site.
Drilling results included one three metre intersection of 10 grams per tonne (g/t), an 11 metre intersection at 2.0 g/t and a three metre intersection at 6.7 g/t.
Howe told Reuters from Johannesburg that because of the low grade of ore detected any operation would have to look at mining four to five million tonnes of ore a year.
He said the grade appeared at this stage to be in the 1.6 to 1.8 g/t range with a cutoff grade of one g/t.
Ghana Gold Mines would know by the end of this year whether the mine would prove economic, but that this was dependent on the gold price, Howe said.
If the gold price was heading towards US$350 an ounce, the project was more likely to be economic, he said.
"At US$300 an ounce, with the capital you'd need for this, you wouldn't push the button on something like this," Howe said.
